name: igus GmbH
summary: Cologne-based German motion-plastics manufacturer whose iglidur tribo-polymer line extends into 3D printing as 'tribo-filament'. Its filaments are engineered for wear resistance, self-lubrication and low friction in functional moving parts — gears, bushings, cable carriers — rather than for general prototyping. Vertically integrated: igus compounds its own polymers and extrudes its own filament.

product_lines.name: iglidur I150-PF
product_lines.notes: Entry-level general-purpose tribo-filament: density 1.3 g/cm3, flexural strength 54 MPa, 65 C continuous / 75 C short-term, up to 50x the abrasion resistance of standard printing plastics; easiest of the range to process on open-frame printers. Base resin undisclosed, so no id is assigned.

product_lines.name: iglidur I151-PF
product_lines.notes: Food-safe variant of I150 (FDA and EU 10/2011 compliant), blue for optical food-safety detection, same ~65 C service temp. Base resin undisclosed.

product_lines.name: iglidur I170-PF
product_lines.notes: Mid-tier grade positioned between I150 and I180. Base resin undisclosed.

product_lines.name: iglidur I180-PF
product_lines.notes: Higher continuous-temperature grade rated to 100 C, for highly dynamic moving applications. Base resin undisclosed.

product_lines.name: iglidur I190-PF
product_lines.notes: Strongest of the I-series: flexural strength 80 MPa, ~50x ABS abrasion resistance, 90 C service temp after tempering; second-strongest tribo-filament after RW370-PF. Base resin undisclosed.

product_lines.name: iglidur J260-PF
product_lines.notes: Workhorse grade: -100 C to +120 C operating range, highest wear resistance and maximum surface speed of the standard tier. Base resin undisclosed.

product_lines.name: iglidur A350-PF
product_lines.notes: Heat-resistant high-performance grade: 180 C continuous service, 340-360 C processing, UL94 V-0, FDA/EU food-contact compliant, requires a heated chamber (min 160 C). The processing window implies a PPS- or high-temp-PA-class base, but igus does not name it.

product_lines.name: iglidur RW370-PF
product_lines.notes: Rail-industry flame-retardant grade: flexural strength 91 MPa, 170 C max application temp, 350-360 C processing, certified to UL94 V-0 and DIN EN 45545. No common-generic equivalent.

product_lines.name: iglidur C210-PF
product_lines.notes: Chemical-resistant tribo-filament for corrosive environments, 260-270 C nozzle. Base resin undisclosed.

product_lines.name: igumid P190-PF
product_lines.notes: Carbon-fiber-reinforced structural filament under the separate igumid sub-brand: flexural strength up to 237 MPa, flexural modulus up to 11.5 GPa, density 1.25 g/cm3, 120 C max long-term. The property profile is consistent with a PA-CF composite, but igus does not state the base resin, so it is left unmapped rather than assigned pa6-cf.

additional_notes: igus's core business is motion-plastics components — plain bearings, cable carriers, linear guides — for automation and industrial markets; 3D printing filament is a materials-sales extension of its self-lubricating polymer competency, serving prototyping and low-volume production of functional parts across food and beverage, medical and manufacturing sectors. Operates a 41,000 sq ft materials test laboratory in Cologne and a US engineering centre in Detroit. igus has manufacturing plants outside Germany, but filament-specific production sites beyond Cologne were not itemised, so manufacturing_countries lists Germany only. Specific filament catalog sub-pages attempted in this session (/product/24471, /wpck/183/3d_druck_filament_engl) returned 404, so only the general 3D-printing materials page is recorded. Also sells SLS powders and DLP resin, which are outside this catalog's scope. No social profiles confirmed. No build-plate or print-surface products — consistent with a materials and components business rather than a printer-hardware vendor. UPDATE (trade-name pass): SKU names are now confirmed from igus product pages (I150-PF, I151-PF, I170-PF, I180-PF, I190-PF, J260-PF, A350-PF, RW370-PF, C210-PF, igumid P190-PF). The previous pa and tpu filament_ids were approximations and have been removed: igus publishes mechanical and thermal data but deliberately withholds base-resin identity for every tribo-filament, so none of them can be mapped to a catalog id with confidence.

provenance.conflicts: No source disagreements, but sourcing is thin: several igus filament sub-pages 404'd and the Wikipedia fetch failed, so SKU names, exact base chemistries (the pa/tpu filament_ids are approximations), non-German filament production and pricing are all unverified.
